title: Larger-first order survived local time swaps in deep ComCat pairs in 2000-2025, but days 1 to 7 gave no clear result
abstract: We tested magnitude order in 785 deep ComCat earthquakes with preferred magnitude at least 5.5 in 2000-2025. We matched locations within each year-month and 500 km, then swapped times within 136 disjoint matches. Magnitudes and locations stayed fixed. Pairs within 200 km and seven days had a signed count of 50: 81 larger-first pairs and 31 smaller-first pairs with magnitude gaps of at least 0.3. The exact expected swap score was 15. In 9,999 draws, the central 95% null range was -4 to 35 and the two-sided p value was 0.0006. The scored pair count changed little, from 109 to 113. Thus the control could change order while it kept most local pair counts. Match distances of 250 and 1,000 km and annual matches gave the same direction of evidence. After exclusion of the first day, the observed score was 14 against an exact mean of 10.5, with p = 0.5194. The data overlap earlier campaign tests. Fair time swaps are a conditional reference, not a physical earthquake model. This result does not prove triggering or dependence between newly drawn magnitudes. Sparse matches, catalog errors and mixed magnitude scales limit use.

display.caption: Observed signed counts and local time-swap references. Gray bars are central 95% null ranges, not confidence intervals for a physical effect.
